:_mod-docs-content-type: CONCEPT

[id="oci-compliant-storage-for-model-registry_{context}"]
= OCI-compliant storage for Model Registry

[role="_abstract"]
You can register and store model artifacts as Open Container Initiative (OCI) images in OCI-compliant registries such as Red Hat Quay.
Storing models as OCI images enables fast deployment with `KServe` by using the `ModelCar` format, which reduces startup times and disk usage compared to traditional S3-based storage.

[id="modelcar-format_{context}"]
== `ModelCar` format

The `ModelCar` format packages model files into a lightweight OCI container image that `KServe` can deploy directly.
Instead of downloading model files from object storage after a container starts, `KServe` pulls the OCI image as part of pod scheduling.
After the initial pull, container runtimes cache the image on the node, so later deployments of the same model version start without an additional download step.

A `ModelCar` image consists of the following layers:

* A minimal base image, such as `busybox`
* Model files layered on top by using OCI Layers On Top (`olot`), a library that the transfer job and Python client use internally to construct the image layers

When you register and store a model as an OCI image, {productname-short} creates the `ModelCar` image automatically.
The resulting artifact URI uses the `oci://` scheme, for example, `oci://quay.io/myorg/granite-7b:v1`.

[id="benefits-of-oci-storage_{context}"]
== Benefits of OCI storage

Storing model artifacts as OCI images provides the following advantages over S3-based or URI-based storage:

Reduced startup times::
`KServe` pulls the OCI image as part of pod scheduling rather than downloading files from an external source after the pod starts.

Lower disk usage::
Pre-fetched OCI images remove the need for local copies of model files on each serving node.

Image caching::
Container runtimes cache OCI images on nodes, so later deployments of the same model version start faster.

Versioned artifacts::
OCI registries offer tagging and versioning for model images, which aligns with container lifecycle management practices.

`KServe` integration::
`KServe` natively supports the `ModelCar` format, so you can deploy models stored as OCI images without additional configuration.

[id="supported-oci-registries_{context}"]
== Supported OCI registries

You can use the following OCI-compliant registries to store model artifacts:

* Red Hat Quay
* Customer-provided OCI-compliant registries that support the OCI Distribution Specification

For Quay destinations, {productname-short} automatically uses `quay.io/quay/busybox:latest` as the base image for `ModelCar` construction.
For other registries, the base image depends on the default configured in the model-sync container.

[id="oci-storage-architecture_{context}"]
== Storage architecture

Model Registry separates model metadata from model artifact storage.
The metadata database stores the model name, version, format, author, and artifact URI, while the actual model files are stored in a separate storage backend.

When you use OCI-compliant storage, the model artifacts are stored as OCI images in a container registry.
The Model Registry metadata entry points to the artifact by using an `oci://` URI.
This separation means you can manage model metadata (versioning, lifecycle, access control) independently from the underlying storage infrastructure.

The model transfer job is a background Kubernetes Job that handles the conversion and push process.
When you register and store a model by using the dashboard, {productname-short} creates a Job in the selected namespace that performs the following steps:

. Downloads the model files from the source location (S3 object storage, URL, or Hugging Face Hub).
. Packages the model files as a `ModelCar` OCI image by layering them on top of a base image.
. Pushes the OCI image to the destination registry.
. Calls the Model Registry API to create the model artifact entry with the `oci://` URI.

The Job creates supporting Kubernetes resources (ConfigMap for model metadata, Secrets for source and destination credentials) that are owned by the Job and garbage-collected when the Job is deleted.

[id="registration-paths_{context}"]
== Registration paths

{productname-short} provides two paths for registering and storing models as OCI images:

Dashboard UI (Register and Store)::
Use the {productname-short} dashboard to register a model from an existing source location, such as S3 object storage or a URL, and transform it into an OCI `ModelCar` image.
The dashboard creates a background Kubernetes Job that copies the model files, packages them as a `ModelCar` image, and pushes the image to the OCI registry.
+
Use this path when your model files are already in S3 storage, a URL, or a model catalog.

Python client SDK::
Use the `model-registry` Python package to upload locally-trained model files directly from your workbench or local environment to an OCI registry.
The Python client uses the `skopeo` or `oras` CLI tool to push the `ModelCar` image.
+
Use this path when your model files are on local disk and are not yet in external storage.
